stories.title: He offered strangers $10 to tie his shoe. Then things got weird
stories.summary: Would $10 convince you to walk up to a stranger and tie their shoe? One Minneapolis artist turned that question into delightfully public chaos.

stories.title: Getting aid to Nepal's flood survivors is the next challenge
stories.summary: The U.S. has pledged 3.5 million in flood aid for Tibet and Nepal, with the first $500,000 distributed by Catholic Relief Services. An aid worker with the group explains what flood survivors need now.

stories.title: Noel Godin, who made powerful people nervous around cream pies, dies at 80
stories.summary: For more than 50 years, Noel Godin went after famous and powerful people with cream pies. His targets included politicians, philosophers, filmmakers and, famously, Bill Gates.

stories.title: The Ukrainian women disappearing into Russian prisons
stories.summary: What happens when Russia arrests civilians in the Ukrainian territories it occupies? New Yorker writer Joshua Yaffa followed a group of women through the Russian prison system.

stories.title: Finally, an economic indicator you can eat
stories.summary: A corn dog may look like lunch. But to an economist, the price is a bigger story about food prices and inflation.

stories.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Telescope begins its journey into deep space
stories.summary: NASA launched a telescope named after Nancy Grace Roman, the pioneering astronomer whose work helped make Hubble and generations of space telescopes possible.
